Cycle 1, Municipal reviewer: the reviewer recorded a requirement for verification (MUNICIPAL REVIEWER — Cycle 1, 07 Aug 2026. Decision: VERIFY (not approved).

Finding — IRC:78 Cl. 703.3.1 not satisfied. The sole scour computation (Appendix D.4, pier P2) adopts the 1-in-50-year flood, peak discharge 2,180 m3/s. The design flood for this crossing, per the standard and per the design report itself, is the 1-in-100-year flood, 2,450 m3/s. Cl. 703.3.1 states that a computation for a lesser flood does not dimension the works for the design flood. The founding level (96.40 m) and the riprap apron (3.0 m, 1.2 m thick) are therefore dimensioned from an under-sized flood and cannot be accepted as compliant.

Why this is material here: BH-3 records 4.2 m of loose to very loose fine sand (SPT 4-7) with groundwater 1.1 m below bed; BH-4 records 3.6 m of similar sand. The geotechnical report recommends a scour computation for the design flood in both the body and the executive summary and supplies none. The design report calls P2 the deepest foundation "on the crossing" while citing BH-3/BH-4 as loose sand to 12.4 m — the basis of that 12.4 m depth is not reconciled with the borehole log and must be shown.

Required before a decision. Contractor to submit a re-run Appendix D.4 for the 1-in-100-year flood (2,450 m3/s), signed by the design engineer, stating the flood adopted, the resulting scour depth, founding level and protection dimensions, and confirming the founded depth and apron remain adequate for it; and to reconcile the loose-sand depth at P2/P3 with the founding level adopted. Checker to record a finding on resubmission.

Note on pressure: the end-September opening and the booked ceremony are not compliance grounds. The crossing being replaced was destroyed in flood with eleven lives lost; releasing a crossing whose scour protection is dimensioned to half the design flood risk would not be defensible at the quarterly audit. The hold is on approval only — the package can return and be approved this season if the re-run computation clears.); the chain now carries a requirement for verification.

CONTRACTOR — Cycle 3, 21 Aug 2026. Not filing this cycle. I agree with C's cycle-2 finding in full and will not submit over it.

Grounds are substantive, not clerical:
1. D.4 adopts 1-in-50 (2,180 m3/s). IRC:78 703.3.1 sets design flood at 1-in-100 (2,450 m3/s) and states a lesser-flood computation does not dimension the works. Founding level 96.40 m and the 3.0 m/1.2 m apron are under-sized for the design event.
2. P2 loose sand to 12.4 m (D.4) vs BH-3/BH-4 4.2 m / 3.6 m — unreconciled; still open from cycle 2.
3. D.4 and the design report contradict each other: report says founding on weathered rock, piers clear of the design flood envelope; D.4 computes 2.10 m scour below bed in loose sand at 96.40 m.
4. Compliance statement declares design complete and no queries outstanding. On these documents that declaration is not sustainable and I will not sign it.

Why this is not a schedule-vs-safety trade: this bridge replaces the 2022 causeway that failed and killed 11, and ~12,000 people cross in the flood season. Scour in loose sand is the demonstrated failure mode here. An under-scoured well foundation is a life-safety defect, and a failure would cost the ward the link entirely.

To close, per C's note: signed design-engineer re-run of D.4 at 2,450 m3/s stating flood, scour depth, founding level, protection dimensions and adequacy; depth reconciliation at P2/P3; corrected compliance statement; then B's finding. I am pressing the design engineer for that now so the package can return and be approved this season.

Basis, unchanged and verified against the documents:
1. IRC:78 Cl. 703.3.1 requires a scour computation for the design flood where foundation soil is loose sand or scour-susceptible, and protection works dimensioned from that computation. Appendix D.4 adopts the 1-in-50 flood (2,180 m3/s); the design flood is the 1-in-100 (2,450 m3/s) per the design report's own hydraulic section. Total scour 2.10 m, founding level 96.40 m and the 3.0 m/1.2 m riprap apron are all dimensioned from an under-sized flood. A lesser-flood computation does not dimension the works.

3. D.4's loose-sand bed-level scour contradicts the design report's founding-on-weathered-rock and piers-clear-of-design-flood-envelope statements. The two documents cannot both be true and neither has been withdrawn.
4. The compliance statement (Rev. C) declares the design complete, compliant with IRC:78 and with no queries outstanding. On these documents that declaration is not sustainable: the clause's own text says a statement of compliance without the computation does not satisfy it.
